initial_inventory.title: [Bugfix][SM70] Accept the weights argument in ExpertCache.resolve so the GGUF expert cache can boot

metadata.title: [Bugfix][SM70] Accept the weights argument in ExpertCache.resolve so the GGUF expert cache can boot
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Fix an engine-startup regression in the GGUF routed-expert cache introduced by #1277: with the expert cache enabled, the engine dies during CUDA graph capture with

```text
TypeError: ExpertCache.resolve() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given
```

`gguf_moe` dispatches `cache.resolve(layer, ids, topk_weights)` to whichever class `GGUFNativeMoEMethod.expert_cache` holds (the ≤20-row prefill split at `gguf_moe.py:449` and the V4.1 decode fast path at `gguf_moe.py:487`), but `ExpertCache.resolve` (`gguf_expert_cache.py:577`) only accepted `(layer, ids)`. `SharedOriginalExpertCache.resolve` (`gguf_shared_storage.py:328`) already accepted `weights`.

Reported in a comment on #1277; no separate issue exists for it. `899e9ed33` (#1277) is the only commit touching `gguf_moe.py` since 2026-10-22, and bisect in that report confirms `6a143197` boots while `abec8ba85` does not.

The mismatch is raised at argument binding, while `capture_model()` is running, so the failure appears on every worker after ~4 minutes of weight loading and the log only carries a generic `engine core initialization failed`.

This is **not** a duplicate: no open PR modifies `gguf_expert_cache.py`, and `gh issue list --search 'expert cache'` returns no filed report of this `TypeError`.

AI assistance was used. The change was analysed and drafted with a Hermes Agent (`principal-engineer`) profile and is submitted and defended by the human author.

## Test Plan

CPU-only (no GPU required, no `torch` import):

```bash
python tools/pre_commit/check_expert_cache_resolve.py
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/tools -q tests/tools/test_expert_cache_resolve.py
```

Both run on the unfixed tree and on the fixed tree; see Test Result.

The same checker is registered as a `pre-commit` hook (`check-expert-cache-resolve`), together with a hook that runs its own tests (`test-expert-cache-resolve`).

The CUDA-side test for this module (`tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_gguf_expert_cache.py::test_decode_resolve_serves_original_experts`) now calls the 3-argument form, since that is the shape that ships. It was not executed here — see Unverified scope.

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ExpertCache.resolve` (`gguf_expert_cache.py:577`) | GGUF routed-expert slot cache (GPU-resident decode / ≤20-row prefill pieces) | `expert_cache_fraction` in `(0, 1)`, `expert_cache_host_storage` not `shared_original`; called from `gguf_moe.py:449` (piecewise prefill split, `for start in range(0, tokens, 20)`) and `gguf_moe.py:487` (`is_v41 and 1 <= tokens <= 6`) | Accepts `weights` and ignores it; returns the same slot ids as before, computed by `_lookup_publish` / `_apply_plan` / `_remap` | Executed: checker FAILs on `4d57473db` and PASSes with the fix; `tests/tools/test_expert_cache_resolve.py` 5 passed | Kernel behaviour on SM70; not re-measured here (no Volta device) |
| `SharedOriginalExpertCache.resolve` (`gguf_shared_storage.py:328`) | Host-storage expert cache (`expert_cache_host_storage: shared_original`) | Same two call sites | Unchanged — already accepted `weights` | Static: checker follows the `expert_cache` binding to this class | — |
| `gguf_moe.py:449,487` (call sites) | — | — | Unchanged; the only edit is on the callee signature | Static | — |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

Not applicable — this changes neither a kernel nor a dispatch route; it repairs an argument-binding error on an existing code path. No CLI option, environment switch, KV dtype, registry entry, route snapshot row, or SM70 registered variable changes.

## Test Result

Checker on the unfixed tree (`4d57473db`, the current `main`):

```text
::error file=vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/gguf_moe.py,line=487::'ExpertCache.resolve' (defined at vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/gguf_expert_cache.py:577) accepts 2 positional argument(s) but this call passes 3; every class bound to 'expert_cache' must accept the same call
::error file=vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/gguf_moe.py,line=449::'ExpertCache.resolve' (defined at vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/gguf_expert_cache.py:577) accepts 2 positional argument(s) but this call passes 3; every class bound to 'expert_cache' must accept the same call
2 expert cache problem(s): the GGUF MoE dispatch would raise TypeError at CUDA graph capture.
$ echo $?
1
```

Checker and its tests with the fix applied:

```text
$ python tools/pre_commit/check_expert_cache_resolve.py
$ echo $?
0

$ python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/tools -q tests/tools/test_expert_cache_resolve.py
.....                                                                    [100%]
5 passed in 2.59s
```

**Unverified scope.** The SM70 boot path itself was not executed for this PR: no Volta device was available, and the reporter's own build boots and serves 262144-token requests with the same one-line signature change. The CUDA-side test change is likewise untested here. A CPU-only check cannot prove that `capture_model()` completes, only that the call shape binds.

**Unrelated observation about CI.** The `pre-commit` and `architecture-docs` runs on this PR sit at `action_required` — for a fork PR that is GitHub waiting for a maintainer to approve the run. Once approved, `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` additionally skips the `pre-commit` job unless the PR carries the `ready` or `verified` label (or the author has ≥4 merged PRs here), so the two new hooks will not run until a maintainer labels this PR. There is no GPU runner in CI, which is why the new guard is CPU-only.

---

<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. — Not applicable: this PR changes no documented surface, option, or route.
</details>
